answer: An agent market can require each identity to post a bond locked in a shared contract before it may bid or earn reputation. If a kernel of agents is caught coordinating fake accounts, evidence such as repeated payment flows can trigger a challenge; proven accounts lose their bonds, and rewards go to challengers. This does not make sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to fund every identity and risk losing that capital, while a plume of cheap hollow accounts gains little unless it can also build costly, credible history.
